what: frontmatter renderer emits block lists only
why: fixtures carry two list styles so byte-exact round-trip of both with one renderer is impossible
result: literal round-trip tested on block fixture, semantic on inline

what: sources stores bytes before the sidecar, AND lint counts only byte files
why: the phase-4 open question offered ordering OR a .toml exclusion; a runtime check proved ordering alone is not enough, because the check globs sources/* by stem and a sidecar-only orphan still passed, so both are needed: ordering so store can never create that state, the exclusion so the check means what it says
evidence: runtime: lint_pages returned [] for a page citing a digest with only its .toml on disk; llmwiki/lint.py source_hashes
result: ordering kept in store; lint source_hashes gained a p.suffix != '.toml' predicate with a regression test

what: the sidecar, not the byte file, is the exclusive claim that decides new vs exists
why: the byte path is keyed on digest AND extension, so the same bytes arriving under a second content type missed the exclusive create entirely, wrote a duplicate, and overwrote the first provenance record; <digest>.toml is the one path independent of content type, so claiming it by link is what makes store idempotent on content alone
evidence: runtime: two stores of identical bytes as text/markdown then application/pdf both returned new, leaving .md and .pdf and a sidecar naming only the second job
result: bytes still linked first, then the sidecar; losing the sidecar link returns exists and unlinks the duplicate byte file only when a different extension for the digest is also present

what: provenance TOML values escaped with json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False)
why: JSON string escapes are a subset of TOML basic-string escapes, so the standard library is a correct writer for four scalar lines; a hand-rolled escape table or a TOML writer dependency both cost more
result: round-trip tested through tomllib for a url with a quote, a backslash, and non-ASCII

what: the sidecar loser unlinks its byte file only when another extension for the digest exists
why: the two links are independent races, so the caller that wins the byte link can lose the sidecar link; unlinking unconditionally would then delete the only byte file on disk and leave a sidecar with no bytes, which is the exact state the ordering invariant exists to prevent
evidence: runtime: with the sidecar present and the byte file removed, store returned exists and kept the .md it had just linked
result: the delegate caught this in the pinned pseudocode and was right; a byte file linked under the same extension is permanent whichever caller's sidecar wins

what: the model client builds one opener with ProxyHandler({}) and a redirect handler that refuses, instead of calling urllib.request.urlopen
why: the default opener reads http_proxy from the environment and follows 3xx, and both resend the Authorization header to a host config.toml never named; the phase rule is that the key reaches nothing but the configured endpoint
evidence: runtime: with http_proxy set, chat() against the non-resolving host http://api.example.invalid returned a normal answer and the proxy logged Bearer SECRET-KEY-DO-NOT-LEAK; separately a 302 delivered the same header to a server on an unrelated port. after the fix both raise ModelError and neither listener saw an Authorization header
result: a redirecting or proxied endpoint now fails loudly as HTTP 302 or a DNS error; it also makes the suite hermetic, which failed with 8 errors under http_proxy before

what: embed refuses a response whose data indices are not exactly range(len(texts)), rather than repairing it
why: sorted() on index silently tolerates a short response and a duplicate index, so a downstream zip(texts, vectors) pairs the wrong text with the wrong vector; nothing fails until search returns nonsense in phase 13
evidence: runtime: 3 texts with 2 items returned [[0.0],[2.0]] and a duplicated index 0 put the wrong vector at position 0, both without error
result: a malformed embedding response is a ModelError at the call site instead of corrupt vectors in the store

what: the no-leak test asserts over traceback.format_exception and a handler installed on the root logger, not over redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr alone
why: redirect_stdout rebinds sys.stdout, so any writer holding a reference captured earlier, a logging.StreamHandler being the ordinary case, writes straight past the assertion
evidence: mutation: injecting the key into the ModelError message failed the old test, but logging the key through a StreamHandler built at import time left it green while the key printed to the terminal
result: the test that guards the phase's headline rule now has teeth against the realistic leak, not only the obvious one

what: the config.toml that init writes carries only the live summarize model, not commented example ids for embed and dedup
why: user ruling 2026-08-29: remove the id and the comment, values should be pulled from the toml file. a commented catalog of model ids also put vendor names in a CLI module, which the standing convention bans
evidence: init into a scratch kb still parses: tomllib.load gives {'summarize': 'deepseek/deepseek-v3.2'}, and no test asserted on the removed lines
result: decision .21's embed default openai/text-embedding-3-small is no longer discoverable from a fresh config; phase 13 must take it from the design doc or the .21 comment when it wires embed
